claims.title: The lowest-type kernel on the whole group
claims.hypotheses: G = U(p,q) is defined by the signature matrix J and K = U(p)×U(q). The parameter λ is strictly decreasing with λ_a − (m−1)/2 integral, μ = λ + ρ, and T is an irreducible K-type of dimension d with unit highest-weight vector w of weight Λ = λ + ρ_n − ρ_c.
claims.statement: The compact average A(x) = d∫_K Φ(k⁻¹xk)T(k)PT(k)⁻¹dk satisfies A(cxc⁻¹) = T(c)A(x)T(c)⁻¹ and A(1) = I. Through the unique polar factorization g = k exp X the kernel Ψ(k exp X) = T(k)A(exp X) satisfies Ψ(k₁gk₂) = T(k₁)Ψ(g)T(k₂) and Ψ(1) = I. Moreover A(exp(−X)) = A(exp X) and Ψ(exp X) is positive semidefinite.
definitions: Φ(Z) = ∏_a Δ_a(Z)^(−(μ_a−μ_{a+1})) with μ_{m+1} = 0 is a product of powers of leading principal minors.
P is orthogonal projection onto ℂw, and K carries Haar measure of mass one.

claims.correspondence: The kernel is the compact average on positive matrices, extended through the polar factors. Its value at the identity uses Schur’s lemma and a trace.
claims.review: The U(1,1) formula, the normalization at the identity and the positivity argument were recomputed independently.

claims.title: A local holomorphic formula for the kernel
claims.hypotheses: The hypotheses of the lowest-type kernel hold with μ = λ + ρ and Λ = λ + ρ_n − ρ_c. A block diagonal matrix has zero entries between opposite signs.
claims.statement: At positive definite x and for block diagonal Y, dA(x)(xY) = −T(Y)A(x) and dA(x)(Yx) = −A(x)T(Y). Both identities persist on a neighbourhood of the positive definite matrices. Near g₀ = k₀ exp X₀ the kernel equals Ψ(g) = T(k₀)A(g⁻¹k₀), so it is the restriction of a holomorphic function and is smooth on G.
definitions: L(B) keeps the entries of B below the diagonal, changes the sign of those above and vanishes on the diagonal.
2ρ_c(a) is the number of later minus the number of earlier positions with the sign of a.

claims.correspondence: The Hermitian identity integrates a pointwise identity whose remaining terms are derivatives along right translations of K. The scalar terms balance exactly when μ = Λ + 2ρ_c.
claims.review: On U(2,1) with λ=(3,1,−2), an exact Haar moment gives dA(I)(2H)=−2H. Replacing μ by Λ gives −2H/3. The integration-by-parts step uses real skew-Hermitian paths before complexifying the differential.

claims.title: The central character of the kernel
claims.hypotheses: The hypotheses of the local holomorphic formula hold.
claims.statement: The quadratic Casimir operator acts on Ψ by |λ|² − |ρ|². Each Gelfand element tr(E^k) acts by γ_k(λ), the coefficient of X^{k+1} in 1 − ∏_r(1 − X/(1 − l_rX)) with l_r = λ_r + (m−1)/2, and the dual family acts by γ_k(−λ). The module generated by the coefficient functions of Ψ therefore has infinitesimal character λ.
definitions: L_X F(z) = dF(z)(Xz) differentiates along left multiplication of the matrix variable.
E_ab is the complex-linear extension of right differentiation on G.

claims.correspondence: The eigenvalue is computed on the minor product, preserved by the compact average and transported to G through the local formula, where the two signs from inversion cancel.
claims.review: Finite differences reproduced the Casimir eigenvalue of the minor product in ranks 2, 3 and 4. The series values at λ = (3/2,−1/2) were recomputed.

claims.title: Decay, Haar integrability and weighted coefficients of the kernel
claims.hypotheses: The hypotheses of the lowest-type kernel hold with q ≥ 1 and opposite-sign gap h. The Haar measure on G is arbitrary.
claims.statement: With t = ‖X‖_F, ‖Ψ(k exp X)‖ ≤ exp(−(h/8)min{t², t/√(2q)}). The kernel is integrable if h > 16mq, square integrable if h > 8mq, and for each real s ≥ 0 the weighted norm ‖Ψ(g)‖²‖g‖_F^s is integrable if h > 8mq + 4s√(2q). If h > max{2m, 16mq + 8√(2q)}, the weighted coefficients ‖g‖_F⟨y,R(g)x⟩ of all generated vectors are square integrable.
definitions: 𝒥(X) = ∏_{a<b} sinh(y_a − y_b)/(y_a − y_b) over the eigenvalues of X is the density of Haar measure in polar coordinates.

claims.correspondence: The decay of the scalar factor passes to the operator norm through positivity. Integrability uses an exponential bound for the polar density.
claims.review: On U(1,1) the exact density and the general threshold were compared directly.

claims.title: Finite spectral decomposition of the column differential
claims.hypotheses: M is the module generated by the kernel coefficients, with Casimir scalar |λ|² − |ρ|², opposite-sign gap greater than 2m and square-integrable weighted coefficients. Columns with entries in M carry the action of V* ⊗ π.
claims.statement: There is a finite set B of real numbers such that every column with entries in M is a finite sum of eigenvectors of D with eigenvalues in B. Every eigenvalue of D on these columns lies in B. The partial trace of D^k is (−1)^k tr(E^k), which acts on M by the coefficient of z^{k+1} in ∏_s(1 + z/(1 − a_s z)) − 1 with a_s = −λ_s − (m−1)/2.
definitions: (Df)_r = −∑_s E_rs f_s, and the tensor Casimir equals the entrywise Casimir plus m + 2D.
Q integrates the squared coefficients of the column action against the vectors y ⊗ e_ξ.
The partial trace of S is x ↦ ∑_c (S(x[c]))_c, where x[c] has x in position c and zeros elsewhere.

claims.correspondence: A finite-dimensional stable piece, a positive invariant form and generation by the lowest-type columns give a vanishing nodal polynomial.
claims.review: The eigenvalues and the partial traces of the powers in the finite model on ℂ² were computed directly and compared with the series.

claims.title: The embedding of a regular shifted model into the columns
claims.hypotheses: λ′ = λ − e_s is a regular lowering, both parameters satisfy the gap and threshold hypotheses, and both kernels are positive on the noncompact part. Their weighted coefficients are square integrable and their generated modules have the central characters of the kernel section.
claims.statement: There is an injective map ι from M′ to the columns with entries in M that commutes with the derivatives and with K, with Dι = a_sι. Every column with Df = a_sf lies in its image. The formal degrees satisfy d′/d = r_s.

claims.correspondence: A Pieri map and a positive pairing give a nonzero projection to the shifted model. Its signed adjoint is the embedding, and the degree defect in both directions fills the eigenspace.
claims.review: In the finite model the two eigenspaces have dimension ratios 1/2 and 3/2, equal to the residues.

claims.title: From an embedding of derivative modules to coefficient identities on the group
claims.hypotheses: ι is an injective map from M′ to the columns that commutes with the derivatives and with K. Both modules are generated by lowest types with Casimir scalars, and both gaps exceed 2m.
claims.statement: For each column f there exists z ∈ M′ such that ∑_c⟨f_c,(A(g)ιx′)_c⟩ = ⟨z,R(g)x′⟩ for every x′ ∈ M′ and every g ∈ G. Conversely, for each z there exists one column f giving the same identity for all x′ and g.

claims.correspondence: The identity is solved at the identity element by compact finiteness, then propagated along one-parameter subgroups by Taylor series with a radius independent of the base point.
claims.review: The radius was checked against the stated layer bound.

classical_references.title: W. Fulton and J. Harris, Representation Theory: A First Course, Springer, 1991, Proposition 15.25 (Pieri's formula for the general linear group)
M. Duflo and C. C. Moore, On the regular representation of a nonunimodular locally compact group, Journal of Functional Analysis 21 (1976), 209–243

outstanding: The realization theorem for the kernel is cited: reproducing formula, irreducibility of the generated module and compact finiteness of its closure. The Pieri rule for compact types and the growth bound for smooth vectors are also cited.
